doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Jazz education and the need to be versatile
summary: Graduates must play many styles, write, and take gigs like weddings; only a tiny fraction become stars.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Do you have your own, I mean you pretty much just said it, do you have your own opinion on the jazz education as a whole in the United States? It’s certainly a big business and there’s a built-in issue with all these graduates, what are they going to do in a business that isn’t as robust as the education.

I think you said it best when you said when we were talking before, you said, this: you’ve got to be versatile. See the days for me, if I could go out and play post-bop like Joe Henderson and those guys, that’s the music that I really love. You’re not going to eat on that. You’ve got to find a way to eat, man. So if Kanye’s got something and he needs a saxophone player to come in to play something, you’ve got to be able to play with him. Or if the symphony is doing a Ravel piece and they need a saxophone player you need to be able to do that. Or if there’s a wedding coming up and you know what, I really don’t like to play weddings but it pays a couple of thousand dollars, you’d be a fool —

That’s right. So they’ve got to look — and they also need to look at skills like writing. You need to — I think the guys that are successful can write a little bit, they play, they’re versatile, and a lot of the different things they can do — because the purists are the guys that have the big names and big jobs is less than one tenth of one percent. You know Wynton and those guys, they’re a very tiny part — of course everybody wants to be like that, but my friend Kevin said his dad J.J. says, he said, “The stars only fall on a few.” And he’s right. So what can I do to make a living doing what I love to do every day. And that’s kind of what I challenge them with.
